page: Amazon Web Services i8ge.metal-48xl is a storage-optimized bare-metal server powered by 192 dedicated physical cores of the AWS ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 processor architecture. Operating at a clock speed of 2.7 GHz, this arm64 platform features 192 single-threaded vCPUs, providing a direct one-to-one mapping of virtual cores to physical hardware. The system is equipped with 1536.0 GB of DDR5 memory, yielding 8.0 GB of RAM per core, and includes a massive 120,000 GB local NVMe SSD storage array. Network connectivity is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 300 Gbps.

Benchmark data highlights top-tier performance in multi-core processing and memory throughput. The server achieves top-tier results in multi-core stress-ng tests, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, and software compilation tasks. Memory bandwidth is exceptionally strong, with read-only cached and uncached operations reaching top-tier classifications, alongside top-tier database operations and Redis SET performance. However, single-core performance and text generation for large language models represent comparative bottlenecks, with LLM text generation for small models scoring in the bottom tier.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the bare-metal configuration offers high resource density, combining massive local NVMe storage capacity with high-speed DDR5 memory. This profile minimizes the overhead of virtualization and maximizes throughput per hardware resource. The server is highly suited for large-scale database deployments, high-throughput Redis caching layers, static web serving, and intensive multi-threaded data processing workloads that require direct access to physical hardware and substantial local storage.
